prompt: Stage 4-5, level 8, 50 gold, 32 HP on a 3-loss streak; the losses cost 12, 13 and 13. Morgana is 1-star with Deathcap, Shojin and Jeweled Gauntlet, with a second copy on the bench; Lillia is 1-star with the tank items. Nobody else plays Coven. Level 9 is 70 XP away. What is the plan for the 50 gold?

lobby.note: Strongest board; you lost 13 to it at 4-3
Beats you; nobody in the lobby plays Coven

options.label: Hold 50 and level 9 at 5-1: a 9-unit board with a 5-cost beats anything you roll into at 8
Roll 20 gold to 30 so you keep 3 interest, and finish the job at 5-1
Roll now to a floor of 10 for Morgana and Lillia 2-star, buy every copy you see, stop the moment both are in
Level 9 is too far to hold for; buy 20 XP toward it and roll the other 30

explanation:
Do the HP arithmetic first. You take 13 a loss: 32 becomes 19 after 4-5 and 6 after 4-6, 4-7 is PvE, and you reach 5-1 with 6 HP where one loss costs 20. So you have exactly two losses left in the game and both are in the next two rounds. That is reason one to break 50: being alive is the game.

The target is concrete: one Morgana, two Lillia. Nobody else is on Coven, so eight Morgana are in the pool; at level 8 a slot is a 4-cost 30% of the time, and with roughly 120 four-cost copies left a specific Morgana is in about 2% of slots, one shop in ten. Forty gold is twenty shops: you find her close to nine times in ten, and usually a Lillia too. Rolling only to 30 keeps 3 gold of interest and halves the shops, turning a 90% rolldown into two in three on the round you cannot miss. Holding for 9 assumes you reach 5-5; you do not. XP adds nothing to a fight that starts in thirty seconds.
principle: Under the two-losses line there is no econ decision left; the whole 50 goes into the fight.
commonMistake: Rolling half the gold to 'keep some interest' when the HP says there is no later round to spend the rest in.
hint: Subtract the damage you have been taking from 32 twice and see which round that leaves you in.
